# Dōbutsu no Mori e+ PC/Android port v0.1.5 (preview)

The sixth preview build of the port that runs [afe-decomp](https://github.com/cailet0422/afe-decomp) (the どうぶつの森 e+ decompilation) on PC and Android.

## Changes since v0.1.4

- **Fixed the 64-bit builds (64-bit Windows, Linux, Android) rarely closing or freezing right after start.**
  - Depending on the memory addresses, which differ on every run, sound data was sometimes read from the wrong place
    (about 1 run in 70).
  - Those addresses were reproduced on purpose; after the fix, the opening and the one-week run are identical to a
    normal run down to the byte.
- Otherwise the same as v0.1.4 (Windows and Linux opening results are identical).
- Signed with the same key as the previous version, so it installs over it (saves and the Korean patch are kept).

### Changes in v0.1.4 (summary)

- Android: fixed the app closing from the next launch on after choosing an MSAA level the device does not support (it
  now starts with a supported level).
- Android: removed the PC settings (Display, Resolution) from the Video tab. Also fixed an internal error on exit and
  restart.

## Read this first

- **No game data is included.** You need your own disc image of the Japanese 「どうぶつの森 e+」 **Rev 1 (GAEJ01)**
  (`.iso` / `.ciso` / `.gcm`) to run it. Disc images are not distributed. This build was made without any assets
  extracted from the disc; it reads them from your own disc image at run time.
- **To play in Korean**, download the Korean patch from [retrodb 한글패치 — 동물의 숲 e+](https://retrodb.info/krpatch/7428/%EB%8F%99%EB%AC%BC%EC%9D%98-%EC%88%B2-e)
  and apply it in the game (below). The Korean patch is the work of an independent author (역전맞고) unrelated to
  this repository; please send questions about the patch to its distribution page. v0.9.2 and v0.9.3 are verified.
- **This is a preview (pre-release).** It has been tested widely on Linux with automated runs and on Android in an emulator, but not yet on real Windows PCs or Android devices.
  Please report problems as issues.

## Files

| File | For |
|---|---|
| `DobutsuNoMoriEPlus-v0.1.5-Windows-x64.zip` | 64-bit Windows. Includes `SDL2.dll`, requires OpenGL 3.3 |
| `DobutsuNoMoriEPlus-v0.1.5-Windows-x86.zip` | 32-bit Windows (also runs on 64-bit Windows). Includes `SDL2.dll`, requires OpenGL 3.3 |
| `DobutsuNoMoriEPlus-v0.1.5-Linux-x86_64.zip` | 64-bit Linux. Requires SDL2 (`libsdl2-2.0-0`) and an OpenGL 3.3 driver |
| `DobutsuNoMoriEPlus-v0.1.5-Android.apk` | Android 5.0 or later, 32/64-bit ARM (armeabi-v7a, arm64-v8a) |
| `SHA256SUMS.txt` | SHA-256 of the files above |

## Running

**Windows / Linux**
1. Unzip the archive, create a `rom` folder inside the extracted `DobutsuNoMoriEPlus` folder and put the disc image in it.
   On Windows you can also pick the folder that holds the image with **Choose folder** in the prompt shown at launch.
2. Run `DobutsuNoMoriEPlus.exe` (Linux: `./DobutsuNoMoriEPlus`).
   Saves are created in `save/` in the same folder.

**Android**
1. Put the disc image in a folder on the phone (e.g. `Download/동물의숲`; the root of `Download` itself cannot be
   picked, so make a folder inside it).
2. Install the APK (allow apps from unknown sources), launch it, and pick that folder with **Choose folder** in the prompt.
3. Both the on-screen (touch) gamepad and physical gamepads work.
4. A release build signed with the release key (certificate SHA-256 `db6fc1ad60b6b6d980bee0990f120ef481f195f117729fa194b124d14752e8b7`).
   It uses the same key as the previous version, so it updates over it. Saves are in the app data folder
   `Android/data/org.afedecomp.dobutsunomori/files/save/`.
5. If the app ends abnormally, the next launch shows a window with the cause before the game starts. Tap
   **복사** (Copy) and paste it into an issue (it is also kept as `crash_prev.txt`). **게임 시작** (Start game)
   starts the game as usual.

**Switching to Korean** (all three platforms)
1. Pause menu (Esc on PC, the Back button on Android) → Settings → **Disc** → **Korean patch: Install**
2. Select the downloaded Korean patch zip as it is (file picker on Windows and Android; on Linux, put the zip in the
   game folder's `patch/`).
3. When it finishes (about a second), choose **Restart now**. The original disc image is not changed; a separate
   Korean image is created in `korean/`. Switch back and forth with **Korean: On / Off** on the same tab.

**Default keys (PC)**: move W/A/S/D, A button Space, B button Left Shift, X and Y, Start Enter, Z, L Q, R E,
C-stick arrow keys, D-pad I/J/K/L. Change them under pause menu → Settings → Controls → Buttons; gamepads work too.
On Korean text-entry screens, type Hangul on a real keyboard with the Dubeolsik (2-set) layout (switch with the
한/영 key, Right Alt or Shift+Space).

## Verified (Linux, automated input scripts)

- New game (Korean name and town name entry) → save → continue, the whole of Nook's part-time job, letters and replies,
  K.K. song requests, house expansion / second floor / basement, round trip to the island, building interiors (shop,
  museum, post office, Able Sisters, police station, villager houses), seasonal events (Harvest Festival, New Year's
  countdown), Redd's tent, the Reset Center, all 15 Famicom games (including saving high scores), a week in a single run.
- The 64-bit build's screenshots and save files are identical to the 32-bit build's, down to the byte. This
  asset-free build also shows the same screens as the regular build.
- The Windows builds (32/64-bit) were checked under Wine: the original-disc opening, a Korean new game, a week in one run
  and the New Year's countdown are identical between the two builds, down to screenshots and saves.
- 64-bit memory placement: with the game memory moved to `0x52000000` and `0x80000000`, the screenshots and saves of the
  opening and of the one-week run stay the same. The arm64 build, run in QEMU with tagged heap pointers like on
  Android, shows the same screens up to the title screen.
- This version's 64/32-bit Windows builds give the same screenshots and saves for the original-disc opening under
  Wine as v0.1.4.
- Android: on an x86_64 emulator (Android 14), verified the disc folder prompt, disc reading (all 17736 assets), the
  opening and the title screen, a crash forced during a run showing up as a report on the next launch, and in the
  game: installing the Korean patch → restart → Korean title screen, and restarting after choosing MSAA 8x (it starts
  with 2x instead).
- GameCube saves (GCI): the repository's `afe_gci` tool imports and exports town saves from a memory card
  (verified: importing a real town GCI → playing and saving → exporting; the tool is not included in this release
  and is built from source).

## Known limitations

- The SD card, GBA link and Card e-Reader are treated as "no device" (the game ends each with its own message).
- Not yet tested on real Windows or Android devices.
- Villagers do not reply to letters with more than a few words of Korean (the Korean patch keeps the code that
  decides this with the Japanese word table; the same happens on a GameCube).
- A save made with the Japanese version and loaded with the Korean-patched disc shows the names stored in the save
  mixed with Hangul characters (the same happens on a GameCube).

Build instructions and detailed progress are in [docs/README.md](https://github.com/cailet0422/afe-port/blob/main/docs/README.md).
